results.name: Agentic Attacks in the Wild: ARTEX & Offensive AI Frameworks
results.description: Between late September and November 2026, cloud environments experienced a surge in automated intrusions driven by agentic offensive frameworks, particularly ARTEX and its variants including Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, and HexStrike. These attacks leverage AI-driven automation to conduct noisy, vector-agnostic campaigns that spray credentials, probe endpoints, and abuse multiple access methods including stolen cloud keys, OAuth flows, and CI/CD trust relationships. Operators route attacks through residential proxy networks making IP-based blocking ineffective. Once initial access is achieved, agents systematically harvest credentials, explore lateral movement opportunities, and exfiltrate sensitive data including API keys and secrets. Poor operational security by attackers has resulted in exposed command-and-control panels revealing both attacker prompts and AI reasoning, providing unprecedented visibility into these machine-speed operations targeting cloud infrastructure and AI platform credentials.

results.name: Vmcloudoor: a stealthy backdoor targeting the Chinese cloud
results.description: A sophisticated Linux implant called Vmcloudoor has been discovered targeting virtual machines hosted on Chinese cloud platforms, specifically Alibaba, Tencent, and Huawei. The backdoor disguises itself by mimicking legitimate cloud service processes and adapts its concealment profile based on the detected environment. It establishes command-and-control communications through Alibaba Cloud infrastructure and Gitee, using time-constrained beacons with machine fingerprinting. The implant features command execution, file transfer capabilities, and system inventory collection. It actively detects security products including EDRs and AVs, adjusting its behavior accordingly. Analysis of the infrastructure suggests development by a Chinese pentester, potentially for red team operations, with evidence pointing to structured development practices and OPSEC failures revealing internal domains and GitHub accounts.

rule vmcloudoor
{
    meta:
        author = "Heurs"
        description = "vmcloudoor / oss_v2 helper: Linux x64 backdoor posing as Aliyun/Tencent/Huawei host agent"
        sample_hash = "0e1bd634d5fc8f4df1c91f0072a4556eb11f41ecc95b05f5a2ffb0e0b914613d"
        date = "2026-10-30"
        source =  "Exatrack"
        tlp =  "CLEAR"
    strings:
        $ns1  = "N6oss_v213OssPullSourceE" ascii
        $ns2  = "N6oss_v216HttpGiteeFetcherE" ascii
        $core = "hpgoc2.oss.v2.core" ascii
        $memfd = "ov2-out" ascii
        $tmp1 = "%s.ov2_%s_XXXXXX" ascii
        $tmp2 = "%s.ov2_%d_%s_XXXXXX" ascii
        $s802 = "unsupported task type in S8-02" ascii
        $gitee = "https://gitee.com/watch_dog_auth/plus/raw/master/config" ascii
        $ua   = "AliyunSysAssist/1.0" ascii
        $p1   = "YunJingSysAssist" ascii
        $p2   = "UniAgentSys" ascii
        $p3   = "kworker/0:2H" ascii
        $shm  = "/dev/shm/.ov2/" ascii
    condition:
        uint32(0) == 0x464c457f and filesize < 3MB and
        ( ($ns1 and $ns2) or $s802 or ($core and $gitee) ) and
        4 of them
}

results.name: MoldyRoost: A Malvertising Machine Built to Deliver iOS Exploits
results.description: MoldyRoost represents a large-scale malvertising operation delivering nation-state-grade iPhone exploit chains through programmatic advertising. Between May and November 2026, over 480 ad domains across six sub-clusters targeted 47 countries, with particular focus on Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, the UK, and Turkey. The operation deploys four exploit kits (Coruna, DarkSword, SilkPath, and GhostWave) through cloaked landing pages that execute drive-by attacks requiring only loading the page on vulnerable iPhones. These kits target iOS versions 13.0 through 26, exploiting multiple zero-day vulnerabilities to exfiltrate cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases, keychain data, messages, and photos. The attackers combine sophisticated cloaking techniques with device fingerprinting to deliver exploits exclusively to iOS devices while showing benign content to others. A leaked repository revealed the operation's infrastructure, including version routers and channel-based attribution systems for stolen credentials.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: The extension you never installed: KREMLIN forges Chrome's own integrity checks to steal banking sessions
results.description: Brazilian banking malware operation REF9334 has been deploying KREMLIN toolkit since May 2025, targeting Brazilian financial institutions through malicious browser extensions. The operation uses multi-stage JavaScript loaders, custom C++ installers, and exploits Chromium integrity mechanisms by manipulating Secure Preferences and regenerating required HMACs. Infrastructure leverages Ethereum smart contracts as dead-drop resolvers for dynamic C2 configuration. Seven distinct campaigns over 15 months show evolution from PULSAR RAT to REMCOS RAT delivery. Attackers impersonate twelve Brazilian banks through Portuguese-language lures, with transaction patterns clustering during São Paulo working hours. The malicious extensions intercept credentials, session tokens, and sensitive banking data through keylogging and request interception capabilities. Over 1,500 infections have been temporarily disrupted through network canary registration, with 98.75% of victims located in Brazil.

results.name: RevStealer Malware: A Hidden Data Heist Behind the Promise of Free AI
results.description: RevStealer is an infostealer first identified in September 2026 targeting Windows systems through trojanized Electron applications disguised as legitimate software, particularly a fake Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop lure. Distributed via GitHub repositories and game-cheat sites, the malware employs sophisticated evasion techniques including anti-debugging, anti-sandbox, anti-VM capabilities, and AES-256-CBC encryption. It conducts comprehensive data theft, harvesting browser credentials, session cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, VPN configurations, Windows Credential Manager data, password managers, messaging applications, and user documents. The malware features encrypted command-and-control communications with blockchain-based fallback using Polygon smart contracts, performs streaming exfiltration of stolen data, and self-deletes to minimize forensic traces rather than maintaining persistence. This rapid theft-focused execution model creates immediate compromise risks with minimal detection windows.

results.name: From Phishing Email to Azalea Agent: Uncovering a Multi-Stage Attack on Ukrainian Government Bodies
results.description: A sophisticated spear-phishing campaign targeted Ukrainian government bodies in October 2026, using a fraudulent email about financial assistance for military unit A1836. The attack employed a RAR archive containing a malicious LNK file that initiated a five-stage infection chain. The sequence began with a curl-based downloader, progressed through multiple encrypted stages including HIODropper and StageLoader, and culminated in the deployment of Azalea Agent 1.21.3, a .NET-based remote access trojan. The campaign utilized a C2 server at 151.244.30.176, historically associated with Iranian ISP Shatel before transitioning to a Canadian ASN. The infrastructure exposed multiple services including OpenSSH, NGINX, RDP, and potentially FRP-based tunneling capabilities. Despite thorough analysis, no definitive attribution to known threat groups was established, as Azalea Agent is a commercially available Malware-as-a-Service tool accessible to multiple operators.

results.name: CLoader Bot Campaign Targets Thai Organizations Through LuaJIT-Based Malware Delivery
results.description: A sophisticated campaign targeting organizations and individuals in Thailand has been identified, utilizing spear-phishing emails to deliver CLoader bot malware through a multi-stage infection chain. The attack begins with an obfuscated JavaScript file disguised as a PDF document using double-extension techniques. This JavaScript drops a LuaJIT executable along with an obfuscated Lua script, which serves as the malware interpreter. The payload employs multiple anti-analysis techniques including UPX packing, resource section obfuscation, and dynamic filename generation. The final payload establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry modifications while masquerading as legitimate Windows services. It communicates with command-and-control infrastructure via Pastebin-hosted configurations and supports remote code execution, PowerShell commands, and Windows Defender exclusion manipulation to evade detection and maintain operational capabilities.

results.name: Lost in relocation: analysis of a new loader distributing CASTLESTEALER
results.description: A previously undocumented Windows loader tracked as OXLOADER delivers the CASTLESTEALER infostealer through malicious Google Ads campaigns. The loader employs sophisticated evasion techniques including control-flow flattening, mixed Boolean-Arithmetic obfuscation, and abuse of the Windows .reloc section to stage shellcode. It incorporates five anti-VM and language checks, self-modifying decryption stubs, and masquerades as legitimate software like Node.js or API Monitor. CIS-region and Russian-language exclusions suggest a financially motivated, Russian-speaking threat actor. The loader achieves low detection rates across static engines and sandboxes, with victims redirected through intermediary domains to Storj-hosted batch scripts that download and execute the payload. The final stage uses DonutLoader to deliver CASTLESTEALER in-memory, targeting credentials and sensitive information.

results.name: Bazuka: The Fraud Framework That Can Do It All
results.description: In late October 2026, a new mobile threat called Bazuka was discovered while investigating an NFC card relay application. Unlike typical banking trojans with simple architectures, Bazuka is a comprehensive modular framework designed for fraudulent operations. The framework consists of a dropper/downloader, core component, and 23 specialized modules covering overlays, keylogging, SMS and 2FA interception, remote control, and cryptocurrency address swapping. Notable features include LLM integration within the control panel to help operators manage infections and identify high-value victims, plus ADB bridging capabilities for covert privilege escalation. Distribution occurs through traffers using lures like adult content, with plans for potential Google Play deployment using minimal permissions to bypass review processes. The control panel, partially in Russian, reveals sophisticated victim management tools and AI-assisted targeting capabilities.

results.name: Rotating Storefronts: Inside a Fake-Shop Network Gearing Up for Black Friday 2026
results.description: A sophisticated fake-shop operation has been identified preparing for Black Friday 2026, utilizing a Chinese-developed SaaS store builder platform called oemcart. The network operates 4,660 domains, with 3,415 observed between October and November 2026, rotating an average of 91 new domains daily. A single storefront was linked to 75 short-lived domains impersonating well-known retailers, primarily targeting Central and Eastern European, UK, and US shoppers. Aldi and Lidl are the most impersonated brands. The operation collects shopper contact details before payment attempts, while payment endpoints are supplied dynamically at checkout to evade detection. Infrastructure rotates between Cloudflare, Tencent Cloud, and Alibaba Cloud. A parallel network of 372 domains impersonates premium fashion brands using WordPress/WooCommerce. The operation employs multiple evasion techniques including daily domain rotation, server-side payment delivery, and CDN usage to hamper traditional detection methods.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
